thread:
customer-prod: Hey team — customers hitting 502/503s when calling /v1/generate across multiple regions since ~08:30 UTC. Sample request_id: req_0a1b2c3d. Response: 'UpstreamError: control-plane 5xx'. High volume but also single-request failures.
maya.chen: thanks for flagging. Are you seeing a spike in latency or auth errors too or strictly 5xx? any correlation with model or region?
customer-prod: mostly 5xx/gateway. No obvious auth 401s in the snapshots I pulled. Happening for both gcp-europe and aws-us-west. We have a few customers reporting timeouts (client 504) and others get immediate 502. Logs attached in support ticket.
jon.patel: @maya.chen grabbing traces now. Can you paste one of the raw response headers or request_id? I want to map to control-plane logs (req_0a1b2c3d).
customer-prod: pasted: `request_id: req_0a1b2c3d`, `x-deployment: hosted-prod`, `model: gpt-open-2024`, `latency_ms: 1200`, response body: `{"error":"UpstreamError","detail":"routing-policy-service returned 500"}`
eli.torres: infra-bot alert: :rotating_light: control-plane: routing-policy-service error rate > 15% over 5m, config-db timeouts observed. Link: http://metrics.internal/alerts/582
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-045 (controlplane-routing-failures). Pager notified.
sre-oncall: I'm on it. Initial hypothesis: routing-policy-service is timing out waiting for config db (configdb) responses, causing 5xx bubbled up to API gateway. Repro steps incoming.
jon.patel: sharing quick repro curl (from inside prod vpc): ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-2024","input":"hello"}'
# response snippet showing 502 and header X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
```
maya.chen: can you check routing-policy logs around that req id? Also check for DB pool exhaustion and slow queries in configdb.
eli.torres: tail from routing-policy: ```
2026-03-15T08:30:12Z ERROR route_eval: timeout contacting configdb (query: select * from routing_policies where tenant_id=...) req=req_0a1b2c3d
2026-03-15T08:30:13Z WARN circuit: upstream timeout after 1.2s, attempts=2
2026-03-15T08:30:13Z ERROR http: returning 502 to api-gateway req=req_0a1b2c3d
```
pri.singh: configdb metrics show connection_pool.waiters spikes and p99 query latency at 950ms. One replica in eu-west was having high IO. I think we're hitting transient DB latency + pool limits.
jon.patel: traced path: api-gateway -> control-plane routing-policy -> configdb. routing-policy has 800ms timeout, but configdb sometimes takes >1s so routing-policy aborts and returns 500 which turns into 502 upstream. Also noticed auth/session checks downstream occasionally return 503 when routing-policy errors, causing mixed 5xxs.
sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options:
- increase routing-policy timeout to 2s and enable a fast fallback route to default policy for critical customers
- add temporary circuit breaker to return cached policy if configdb fails
- scale up configdb read replica for eu-west and increase DB conn pool size
- communicate to affected tenants
eli.torres: I'll push a config flip to enable cached-fallback for 10% of traffic for 30m. Command: `kubectl set env deploy/routing-policy CACHE_FALLBACK=enabled --namespace prod`
maya.chen: @eli.torres please also add extra logging for pool waiters and tag with tenant ids so we can identify noisy customers.
pri.singh: scaling configdb read replica now (provisioning). Also increasing postgres max_connections and the proxy pool size.
sre-oncall: rolling restart of routing-policy not recommended yet — prefer config flips first. If error rate persists after cache_fallback, do canary restart of 3/10 pods.
customer-prod: thanks. Customers still seeing errors but volume dropped after ~10:05 UTC when cache_fallback rolled out. We still have a small tail.
jon.patel: long-term fixes to track in ticket: (1) query timeouts + retry strategy tuning between routing-policy and configdb; (2) add local LRU caching per routing-policy pod (3) better circuit-breaker with stale-but-safe fallback policies; (4) observability: alert on configdb waiter-count crossing 50.
maya.chen: notes for customer comms: apologize, say root cause was transient config-db latency causing routing-policy to return 5xx, mitigation: enabled cached fallback and scaled replicas, ETA for full resolution 3 hours. Offer credit for incident window. Draft: "We experienced transient control-plane failures due to config DB timeouts which impacted routing decisions resulting in 5xx for API requests. We applied a cached fallback and scaled storage to restore service. We're investigating permanent fixes and will follow up with a postmortem."
eli.torres: post-incident tasks: create runbook entry for routing-policy DB backpressure, add automated fallback config rollout job, add synthetic tests hitting routing-policy-cached paths.
pri.singh: monitoring: added new metric `configdb.connection_pool_waiters` and a Grafana panel. Alert threshold: >40 sustain 3m. Also added runbook link.
customer-prod: appreciate the fast triage. Will update customers and close ticket when you confirm stable.
sre-oncall: marking incident as mitigated in INC-2026-045. Follow-up owner: pri.singh for DB work, jon.patel for routing-policy code changes, maya.chen for customer comms. :thumbsup:
maya.chen: closing loop: 13:00 UTC postmortem scheduled, will attach logs and timeline. Thanks team.
